ds: Cash-intensive businesses underreport takings through suppressed sales records, electronic sales suppression tools or diverting cash from the till. The unreported cash is spent outside the banking system, deposited in structured amounts or moved offshore.

OECD, Shining Light on the Shadow Economy: Opportunities and Threats (2017)

cn.rt: Small cash business owners structure skimmed takings into personal everyday accounts, mainly via branch cash deposits.

rat: Cash-intensive business sales suppression, structured deposits.

ind.n: Declared turnover lower than card and bank takings imply
ind.cx: Card acquiring volumes or supplier purchases suggest higher sales than the business reports to authorities.
ind.fp: Timing differences, refunds and tips affect reconciliation.
ind.ds: Card acquiring volumes or supplier purchases suggest higher sales than the business reports to authorities.

ind.n: Cash deposits well below expected for business type
ind.cx: A business with high card use but little cash banking, despite sector norms of cash trade.
ind.fp: Cash may be used to pay suppliers legitimately.
ind.ds: A business with high card use but little cash banking, despite sector norms of cash trade.

ind.n: Cash used to pay suppliers and wages directly
ind.cx: Owner pays suppliers, rent or staff in cash taken from takings before banking.
ind.fp: Small suppliers sometimes insist on cash.
ind.ds: Owner pays suppliers, rent or staff in cash taken from takings before banking.

ind.n: Structured cash deposits across branches or accounts
ind.cx: Cash banked in many amounts just below reporting thresholds, often across multiple branches or personal accounts.
ind.fp: Some businesses make routine daily deposits in small sums.
ind.ds: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
ind.cn: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts

ind.n: POS software with sales-suppression features or tampered records
ind.cx: Use of unfamiliar till software, offline mode usage, or missing sequential receipts.
ind.fp: Software glitches or offline trading can cause gaps.
ind.ds: Use of unfamiliar till software, offline mode usage, or missing sequential receipts.

ind.n: High refund or void rates on card terminals
ind.cx: Frequent voids and cash refunds conceal sales.
ind.ds: Frequent voids and cash refunds conceal sales.

ind.n: Owner lifestyle inconsistent with declared profits
ind.cx: Spending, assets and property purchases exceed what reported profits could support.
ind.fp: Family wealth or gifts could explain this.
ind.ds: Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
ind.cn: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means

ind.n: Cash transferred to offshore through MVTS or cash couriers
ind.cx: Cash takings leave the country via money transfer, hawala-style networks or couriers.
ind.fp: Diaspora remittance is common and lawful.
ind.ds: Cash takings leave the country via money transfer, hawala-style networks or couriers.

ctl.ds: Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.
Compares account flows with filed accounts, VAT or sales tax data and tax remittances, and links to VAT-fraud controls. It spots under-declared revenue and tax fraud proceeds.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

ctl.n: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
ctl.ds: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Verifies merchant identity, business model, website content and expected volumes before activation and re-verifies on change, with remediation of weak merchants. It stops fronts and disguised businesses entering payment channels.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

Establishes how a customer accumulated their overall wealth and corroborates it with independent evidence rather than relying on self-declaration. It is central to managing high-net-worth, politically exposed and high-value-purchase relationships.

ctl.n: Cash exchange, declaration and courier checks
ctl.ds: Collects identification for cash exchange, cross-checks cross-border cash declarations, screens freight, mail and cash-in-transit use and applies courier intelligence. It addresses bulk cash movement across borders.
